In practice, dropout = 0.0 means dropout is disabled, so the layer has no effect during training or inference. Many researchers include dropout as a hyperparameter in their experiments and report that the optimal value found was 0.0.
Examples of how to report it:
"The dropout rate was tuned over {0.0, 0.2, 0.5}. The best validation performance was achieved with a dropout rate of 0.0."
or
"No dropout regularization was applied (dropout = 0.0)."
